extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: WikiText is a language modeling dataset extracted from verified Good and Featured articles on Wikipedia. It is provided in two sizes: WikiText-2 (over 2 million tokens, vocabulary of 33,278) and WikiText-103 (over 103 million tokens, vocabulary of 267,735). Both datasets feature punctuation, original casing, a larger vocabulary, and numbers, making them more realistic for real language use compared to Penn Treebank. The dataset was constructed to enable the learning and evaluation of longer term dependencies in language modeling.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher (MetaMind - A Salesforce Company)
extraction.citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., & Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:1609.07843.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Articles were selected from Wikipedia fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors. These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text extracted from Wikipedia articles classified as Good or Featured articles, obtained via the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Minor bugs such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from HTML were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracting the raw text from Wikipedia mark-up required handling many macros (metric conversion, abbreviations, language notation, date handling). Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, slightly augmented to further split numbers (e.g., 8,600 -> 8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor fixes. Following Chelba et al. (2013), a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token. The dataset is provided in the same format and following the same conventions as the PTB dataset.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available in two different sizes: WikiText-2 and WikiText-103. Both datasets use the same articles for validation and testing with the only difference being the vocabularies.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Penn Treebank (compared against) has limitations including lower-cased tokens, stripped punctuation, and limited 10k vocabulary. WikiText addresses these but other large-scale datasets have restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering which is unrealistic for most language use.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Language modeling benchmark for training, validation, and testing. Designed to serve as a platform to improve handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling.
